question: Where should eye drops be placed when instilling medication into the eye?

options.A: Underneath the upper eyelid margin
options.B: Into the inner corner near the nose
options.C: Into the lower conjunctival sac
options.D: Directly onto the center of the cornea

explanation: The conjunctival pocket holds the drop safely on the eye surface without harming the sensitive cornea. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is the term for the unwritten social rules about how men and women should behave?

options.A: Biological sex
options.B: Genetic traits
options.C: Gender norms
options.D: Chromosomal codes

explanation: Gender norms are societal expectations that dictate acceptable behaviors and roles for different genders within a specific culture. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which type of study collects data at just one single point in time?

options.A: Longitudinal study
options.B: Experimental trial
options.C: Cross-sectional study
options.D: Prospective cohort study

explanation: You've got this! A cross-sectional study is like taking a quick photograph—it gathers all the data from people at one specific moment.

question: What do blood vessels in the skin do when your body needs to release extra heat?

options.A: They dilate (widen)
options.B: They calcify
options.C: They rupture
options.D: They constrict (narrow)

explanation: Spot on! When they widen (dilate), warm blood moves closer to the skin surface so excess body heat can escape into the air. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main goal of health education in nursing?

options.A: Fulfilling mandatory legal paperwork
options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital equipment
options.C: Diagnosing complex medical conditions
options.D: Promoting health and preventing disease

explanation: Spot on! Our core job as nurses is to help people stay well and stop illnesses before they even start. Keep it up!

question: Why is an individualized care plan so important in rehabilitation?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to document patient progress.
options.B: Patients with the same medical diagnosis can have completely different functional abilities and personal goals.
options.C: Insurance companies refuse to pay for care plans that mention physical therapy.
options.D: Standardized care plans are illegal in specialized hospital settings.

explanation: Exactly! No two patients are alike, even with the same diagnosis. Their care must fit their unique lifestyle, support system, and personal goals.

question: Why are individuals with pre-existing mental health conditions especially vulnerable during disasters?

options.A: They are completely immune to physical injuries
options.B: Disasters automatically cure their psychiatric symptoms
options.C: Their usual support systems and medication routines are often disrupted
options.D: Emergency workers always prioritize them over everyone else

explanation: When clinics close, pharmacies run out of stock, and daily structures collapse, stable mental health conditions can quickly deteriorate. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h4)

question: Why does a lower pH number mean higher acidity?

options.A: A lower number shows that bicarbonate levels have increased
options.B: A lower number indicates fewer metabolic wastes in the plasma
options.C: A lower number represents a complete lack of dissolved gases
options.D: A lower number means a higher amount of free hydrogen ions

explanation: Think of it this way: the more free hydrogen ions pile up, the more acidic the fluid becomes, and the lower the pH number drops. You've got this!

question: What should a nurse do FIRST when an Alzheimer's patient suddenly becomes aggressive?

options.A: Immediately request a strong prescription sedative from the doctor
options.B: Look for unmet physical needs or triggers in the environment
options.C: Scold the patient firmly to stop the unacceptable behavior
options.D: Isolate the patient in a quiet, dark room until they fall asleep

explanation: You got it! Agitation is often how they express pain, hunger, or fear. Finding and fixing the trigger is always our best first nursing action!

question: What practical tool can a nurse recommend to help an elderly patient who forgets daily doses?

options.A: A strict fasting diet plan
options.B: A weekly pill organizer box
options.C: A large wall calendar for appointments
options.D: A daily rigorous exercise chart

explanation: Pill boxes sorted by day and time help patients easily see whether they have taken their scheduled medications. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h7)

question: How does a 'just culture' help a hospital reduce unwanted variation in care?

options.A: By punishing anyone who deviates from standard hospital routine
options.B: By ensuring every nurse receives the exact same annual salary bonus
options.C: By removing all nursing supervisors from clinical hospital wards
options.D: By encouraging staff to report workflow issues and near-misses safely

explanation: You're a star! A just culture builds trust so nurses feel safe speaking up about problems before anyone gets hurt. Keep up the awesome work!

question: What should a nurse focus on when assessing a pregnant patient for constipation?

options.A: The blood pressure reading taken in the right arm
options.B: Exclusively the heartbeat of the developing fetus
options.C: Stool consistency, straining effort, and dietary habits
options.D: Only the exact weight of the patient on the scale

explanation: Spot on! To truly help, we need to ask about how hard the stool is, if she struggles to push, and what she's been eating and drinking.

question: Which monitoring method provides the only true proof that sterilization successfully killed all bacterial spores?

options.A: Chemical indicator tape
options.B: Visual inspection for rust
options.C: Mechanical pressure gauges
options.D: Biological indicators

explanation: Biological indicators use actual heat-resistant bacterial spores to verify that the machine successfully destroyed all microbial life. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h4)

question: Why do your hands and lips take up so much more space on the brain's sensory map than your back or thighs?

options.A: The cerebral cortex processes touch differently in the lower body.
options.B: Skin on the back has thicker layers of subcutaneous fat.
options.C: Signals from the upper limbs travel faster than spinal signals.
options.D: The hands and lips contain a much higher density of sensory receptors.

explanation: Well done! Parts of the body that need super-fine touch discrimination require more brain power, giving them a much bigger spot on the sensory homunculus.

question: Why do DRF programs love buying drugs by their generic names?

options.A: Patients refuse to take medications with brand names
options.B: Generic drugs do not require any regulatory inspection
options.C: Generic drugs are much cheaper than branded equivalents
options.D: Generic medications never expire on hospital pharmacy shelves

explanation: Generic drugs give us the same medical power as expensive brand names, but at a much lower cost—helping keep healthcare affordable for everyone.

question: What is the main purpose of agricultural subsidies provided by the government?

options.A: To lower production risks and support farmers
options.B: To replace natural rainfall with artificial irrigation everywhere
options.C: To increase the retail price of basic food items
options.D: To punish farmers who grow traditional local crops

explanation: Subsidies help farmers manage financial and environmental risks so they can keep producing food reliably. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h3)

question: Which tech allows a patient to send recorded data, like a photo of a rash, for a doctor to check later?

options.A: Real-time interactive
options.B: Store-and-forward
options.C: Remote patient monitoring
options.D: Synchronous conferencing

explanation: 'Store-and-forward' means you save the information (like a photo or test result) and send it for a provider to review whenever they have a moment. No live video needed!

question: Why is partner notification and treatment a must when managing STIs?

options.A: To punish individuals who engage in unprotected sexual intercourse
options.B: To determine which partner originally contracted the infection first
options.C: To prevent reinfection and break the ongoing cycle of transmission
options.D: To fulfill mandatory insurance reporting requirements for hospitals

explanation: If you treat only one partner, they will just catch the infection right back the next time they have sex. Both partners must be treated together to truly heal!

question: Which of these is NOT part of a standard school health program?

options.A: Health instruction and education
options.B: School health services
options.C: Advanced neurosurgical training
options.D: Healthy school environment

explanation: Correct! Brain surgery is specialized hospital care, way beyond what a primary school health program needs or does.

question: A new mother is worried about straining on the toilet with her stitches. What is the best advice to give her?

options.A: Restrict fluid intake so you do not need to go as often
options.B: Avoid eating solid food for the first two weeks
options.C: Hold your breath and push firmly to finish quickly
options.D: Eat plenty of high-fiber foods and drink plenty of fluids

explanation: Wonderful advice! Fiber and water keep stools soft, preventing constipation so she won't have to strain and hurt her healing tissues.

question: What happens to the total drug effect during synergism?

options.A: It drops lower than the effect of either single drug
options.B: It equals the exact sum of both individual effects
options.C: It becomes greater than the sum of the individual effects
options.D: It completely cancels out any therapeutic benefit

explanation: Think of synergism like teamwork! When two drugs work together synergistically, their combined power is much greater than what each could ever do on its own.

question: What is the primary surgical treatment for uterine cancer?

options.A: Total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
options.B: Partial resection of the uterine cervix only
options.C: Removal of both ovaries while leaving the uterus intact
options.D: Cryotherapy and laser ablation of the endometrium

explanation: You got it! Standard surgery means taking out the uterus, Fallopian tubes, and ovaries to treat the cancer safely.

question: What is the main purpose of an action plan during a project?

options.A: To raise funds from international organizations after the event
options.B: To change the objectives after the project has already started
options.C: To outline who is responsible for each task, the timeline, and required resources
options.D: To grade community members based on their health test scores

explanation: An action plan keeps everyone organized. It clearly shows who is doing what, when they are doing it, and what tools they need.

question: In the chain of infection, which link do you break directly every time you wash your hands?

options.A: Infectious agent
options.B: Reservoir
options.C: Susceptible host
options.D: Mode of transmission

explanation: Spot on! Since your hands act as the vehicle carrying germs around, washing them stops the journey dead in its tracks.

question: What is the primary goal of nutrition counselling in primary health care?

options.A: Guiding food choices to promote health and prevent disease
options.B: Prescribing expensive nutritional supplements for every patient
options.C: Enforcing strict hospital dietary restrictions on communities
options.D: Diagnosing rare metabolic disorders in a laboratory setting

explanation: Nutrition counselling focuses on helping clients make healthy food choices to prevent illness and support overall wellness in primary care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h1)

question: What is the primary danger associated with polypharmacy in older patients?

options.A: Complete elimination of side effects from strong painkillers
options.B: A high likelihood of adverse drug reactions and harmful interactions
options.C: Rapid improvement in cognitive processing speed and memory
options.D: Immediate cure of all existing chronic and acute health conditions

explanation: Taking many different medicines at once greatly increases the chance that they will interact badly with each other or cause harmful side effects. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h6)

question: What should happen immediately after identifying gaps in a nursing audit?

options.A: Destroying all patient records to protect staff privacy
options.B: Stopping all patient admissions to the hospital
options.C: Implementing corrective actions to improve the care
options.D: Firing all nursing supervisors on the affected ward

explanation: That's right! Audits are meant to spark positive change, so we must put practical solutions in place right away to fix what was broken.

question: What is a common mistake nurses should avoid when suspecting a notifiable disease outbreak?

options.A: Informing the local government health team too quickly
options.B: Using standard case definition sheets during patient assessment
options.C: Waiting for full laboratory confirmation before reporting the suspect case
options.D: Submitting weekly summary logs to public health authorities

explanation: Never wait for lab results if you suspect a dangerous outbreak! Report based on clinical signs right away so health teams can act fast.

question: What is the name of the hollow ball of cells that travels down to plant itself in the uterus?

options.A: Blastocyst
options.B: Gamete
options.C: Zygote
options.D: Morula

explanation: By the time it's ready to nestle into the uterine lining, the tiny group of cells is called a blastocyst. You're doing brilliantly!

question: A student has stomach cramps and diarrhea after drinking from the school tap. Which part of the school environment failed here?

options.A: Academic evaluation standards
options.B: Physical environment safety
options.C: Psychosocial climate safety
options.D: Curriculum design policy

explanation: Well done! Safe drinking water is a basic part of the physical school environment, so bad water means a breakdown in physical safety.

question: Why must you store your interview audio files and transcripts in password-protected digital folders?

options.A: To prevent accidental loss of data and protect patient confidentiality
options.B: To speed up the internet connection in the research office
options.C: To make the files look more professional for publishing
options.D: To allow the general public to read private hospital stories

explanation: Exactly right! Patient stories are deeply personal, and keeping digital files secure is a core part of ethical nursing practice.

question: A patient has a stiff, painful knee joint. Which membrane inside the joint is likely failing to produce enough lubricating fluid?

options.A: Cutaneous membrane
options.B: Synovial membrane
options.C: Serous membrane
options.D: Mucous membrane

explanation: Synovial membranes line our movable joints and pump out synovial fluid to keep movements smooth and pain-free.

question: Why do tablets or injections (systemic drugs) often struggle to treat eye problems effectively?

options.A: Blood vessels in the eye destroy active ingredients
options.B: Unique barriers like the cornea block them from getting inside
options.C: Systemic drugs cannot dissolve in body fluids
options.D: The liver breaks down all eye medications too quickly

explanation: Think of the eye as a well-guarded fort! Natural barriers like the cornea make it hard for drugs travelling through your bloodstream to get inside the eye in strong enough amounts.

question: What type of data is mostly used in explanatory research designs?

options.A: Numerical measurements and statistical testing
options.B: Only handwritten personal diaries from patients
options.C: Random historical fiction books
options.D: Unstructured gossip from hospital hallways

explanation: Well done! Explanatory designs use numbers and statistics to clearly show cause-and-effect links.

question: What is the main heart and philosophy behind home health nursing?

options.A: Promoting patient empowerment and self-care within their environment
options.B: Isolating the patient from family members to prevent infection
options.C: Transferring all decision-making power entirely to the physician
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital routines inside private residences

explanation: Well done! It's all about helping patients and their families feel confident to manage their own health right where they live.

question: A patient just had pituitary surgery and is now peeing out 500 mL of very clear, watery urine every single hour, and their blood sodium is climbing. What is happening?

options.A: Syndrome of inappropriate ADH (SIADH)
options.B: Diabetes insipidus
options.C: Acute adrenal crisis
options.D: Cushing's syndrome

explanation: That massive output of dilute urine right after pituitary surgery is the classic hallmark of diabetes insipidus. The gland is stunned and temporarily (or permanently) stops making enough ADH.

question: Why do registered nurses practice delegation during a heavy shift?

options.A: To manage heavy workloads and provide safe, efficient care
options.B: To shift legal blame for mistakes onto junior support staff
options.C: To comply with government orders regarding hospital staffing ratios
options.D: To avoid performing direct physical care for stable patients

explanation: Delegation isn't about passing work away because you're lazy—it's a smart teamwork tool to ensure every patient gets safe, timely care.

question: What is an important preventive screening topic for women receiving long-term home health care?

options.A: Daily testing for adult growth hormone levels
options.B: Mammogram schedules and breast self-awareness
options.C: Monthly surgical checks for joint replacement
options.D: Weekly testing for acute kidney stone formation

explanation: Regular breast screenings and awareness are key components of preventive health maintenance for adult women. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h7)

question: A community links weight gain with high social status, making residents resistant to weight-loss advice. What is the best nursing approach?

options.A: Reframing the message around maintaining physical strength and caring for grandchildren
options.B: Stopping health education entirely until local cultural traditions change
options.C: Focusing solely on prescription weight-loss medications available at the pharmacy
options.D: Telling them bluntly that their cultural beliefs are outdated and dangerous

explanation: Smart nursing! Good community nurses respect local culture while gently connecting healthy habits to things the people already care about deeply, like family.

question: Which sign is most characteristic of a tension pneumothorax?

options.A: Frequent coughing with clear, thin mucus production
options.B: A slow and steady heart rate with warm, dry skin
options.C: Absent breath sounds on the affected side of the chest
options.D: Equal and bilateral chest expansion during breathing

explanation: Trapped air collapses the lung and prevents air entry, resulting in absent or significantly diminished breath sounds on that side. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h4)

question: What is the primary job of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) in the body?

options.A: Regulating the baseline basal metabolic rate of body cells
options.B: Releasing emergency calcium from bones during muscle tetany
options.C: Triggering water reabsorption in the kidney collecting ducts
options.D: Lowering sudden spikes in blood glucose after carbohydrate intake

explanation: T3 and T4 act like your body's engine idle speed, controlling how fast your cells burn energy and use oxygen every day.

question: How can a nurse best support self-advocacy in a patient with a physical disability?

options.A: By making all medical and lifestyle decisions on behalf of the patient
options.B: By encouraging the patient to voice their own healthcare choices and rights
options.C: By shielding the patient from interacting with unfamiliar community members
options.D: By filing formal legal complaints without consulting the patient first

explanation: Self-advocacy grows when nurses empower patients to speak up and make their own informed decisions about care and life. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h8)

question: What is the main difference between endocrine and exocrine glands?

options.A: Endocrine glands lack ducts and release hormones directly into the blood
options.B: Exocrine glands possess a rich network of fenestrated capillaries
options.C: Endocrine glands secrete substances exclusively onto the skin surface
options.D: Exocrine glands produce chemical messengers while endocrine glands do not

explanation: Think of endocrine glands as ductless delivery systems! Because they don't have tubes (ducts), they dump their hormones straight into the bloodstream to travel round the body. You've got this!

question: Which group of people faces a much higher risk of experiencing interpersonal violence?

options.A: Retired corporate executives
options.B: Middle-aged professional athletes
options.C: Pregnant women and young children
options.D: Healthy young adult males living by themselves

explanation: You got it! Vulnerable groups like pregnant women, children, and older adults statistically experience higher rates of abuse and neglect.

question: A nurse organizes a stress-management workshop for workers facing imminent factory closures. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Secondary prevention
options.D: Curative prevention

explanation: Spot on! Primary prevention focuses on stopping health problems before they start by promoting healthy coping strategies early on. Excellent! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h5)

question: Why would a nurse researcher go for a correlational design?

options.A: To randomly assign patients to different hospital diets
options.B: To prove that variable A causes variable B to change
options.C: To test the effectiveness of a brand-new surgical tool
options.D: To explore the relationship between two existing variables

explanation: You got it! Correlation checks how two things relate to each other (like stress and lack of sleep), without claiming one directly causes the other.

question: You are bagging an unresponsive patient with a bag-valve-mask, but their chest isn't rising. What should you do next?

options.A: Disconnect the oxygen tubing from the wall supply
options.B: Turn the patient onto their side in the recovery position
options.C: Squeeze the ventilation bag much harder and faster
options.D: Reposition the head and check the airway for blockage

explanation: If air isn't going in, don't just squeeze harder! Check for a blockage and readjust the head position to open up that airway properly. You're doing great.

question: Why do community nurses rely heavily on basic anthropometric tools like measuring tapes?

options.A: Advanced hospital equipment is always brought to the field
options.B: Blood tests are illegal outside of licensed hospitals
options.C: Patients prefer tape measurements over physical examinations
options.D: They allow quick screening of large populations in remote areas

explanation: Remote clinics lack heavy laboratory equipment, so nurses use simple tools to screen many people efficiently. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h1)

question: What usually happens during the orientation phase of meeting a patient?

options.A: Rapport is built and the purpose of the interview is explained
options.B: The nurse summarizes all findings and leaves the room
options.C: The patient is discharged with written medication instructions
options.D: Detailed physical assessments and vital signs are finalized

explanation: Correct! The orientation phase is all about friendly introductions, setting expectations, and building that initial trust.

question: When should a nurse refer a postpartum mother to a specialized family planning clinic?

options.A: When a new mother refuses to hold her baby after a normal delivery
options.B: When routine postpartum lochia transitions from red to yellow-white
options.C: When the infant develops mild neonatal jaundice in the first week
options.D: When a client has a complex medical history requiring expert evaluation

explanation: Mums with underlying health conditions like severe high blood pressure need expert guidance to pick the safest contraceptive method.

question: Which liver enzyme is known to be more specific to liver cell injury?

options.A: AST
options.B: Amylase
options.C: ALT
options.D: Lipase

explanation: Spot on! Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) is concentrated mostly inside liver cells, making it a reliable red flag when liver tissue is damaged.

question: Why is vitamin K given as an injection to a newborn baby?

options.A: To treat neonatal jaundice caused by blood incompatibility
options.B: To prevent bleeding disorders due to immature clotting factors
options.C: To stimulate spontaneous crying and lung expansion
options.D: To protect the infant against bacterial eye infections

explanation: You got it! A newborn's tummy is sterile and doesn't make vitamin K yet, so this shot protects them from dangerous bleeding.

question: In Nigerian homes, which household liquid is most often accidentally swallowed by children because it's stored in empty drink bottles?

options.A: Clean water
options.B: Cooking oil
options.C: Fruit juice
options.D: Kerosene

explanation: Well done! Storing kerosene in old soft drink bottles is a major hazard because kids easily mistake it for water or juice.

question: Which hormone directly builds up and thickens the uterine lining during the first half of the cycle?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Think of estrogen as the builder hormone! Produced by the growing follicles, it helps rebuild and thicken the endometrium after a period ends.

question: A young football player just finished a tough 90-minute match. What kind of snack is best for quick recovery?

options.A: A mix of carbohydrates and protein
options.B: Only pure fat sources like butter
options.C: A heavy meal high in saturated fat
options.D: Plain carbonated water with no nutrients

explanation: Spot on! Carbs quickly refill empty energy tanks, while protein helps repair tired muscles after a heavy game.

question: Why do droplet precautions require masks only when close to the patient?

options.A: Droplet germs disappear completely after three minutes
options.B: Large droplets fall quickly to the ground within a short distance
options.C: Masks stop working if you walk past three feet
options.D: Germs in droplets cannot survive inside a hospital

explanation: Unlike tiny airborne particles, heavy respiratory droplets drop out of the air quickly, usually within three feet of the source. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h4)

question: Which ethical principle means a nurse should actively do good and help the patient?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Beneficence
options.D: Justice

explanation: Nailed it! 'Beneficence' comes from words meaning to do good. It's your daily push as a nurse to take positive actions that genuinely help your patients.

question: What is an epitope?

options.A: An organ responsible for filtering red blood cells
options.B: The specific part of an antigen that an antibody binds to
options.C: A white blood cell that destroys bacteria in the bloodstream
options.D: A chemical medication used to suppress severe allergies

explanation: An epitope is like the specific 'handle' or grip on the antigen that antibodies lock onto.

question: Why is herd immunity so helpful for vulnerable people in a community?

options.A: It guarantees that every single person in the population will develop permanent natural immunity
options.B: It completely eliminates all known environmental reservoirs of a bacterial pathogen
options.C: It transforms live vaccines into safer, non-replicating subunit vaccines
options.D: It reduces overall disease spread, indirectly protecting those who cannot be vaccinated

explanation: Brilliant! When most people are vaccinated, germs struggle to spread, keeping even the unvaccinated safe.

question: What is a major goal of any good pharmacovigilance program?

options.A: Increasing the profit margins of local drug manufacturing plants
options.B: Early detection of unknown or rare adverse drug reactions
options.C: Lowering the market price of essential pharmaceutical goods
options.D: Replacing traditional clinical trials with computer simulations

explanation: Well done! Catching safety warning signs early is key to making sure patients stay safe from unexpected harm.

question: Why does spending most of a health budget on recurrent costs (like salaries) hurt long-term care?

options.A: It stops international donors from sending vaccines to the country
options.B: It forces hospitals to close down outpatient departments permanently
options.C: It leaves very little money for capital investments like equipment and infrastructure
options.D: It prevents clinical nurses from receiving their monthly salaries on time

explanation: If all the money goes straight to paying overhead and salaries, there's little left over to buy new machines, build wards, or upgrade facilities.

question: How would you best describe a 'geopolitical' community?

options.A: A religious group meeting across multiple countries
options.B: An online forum for chronic disease support
options.C: Physical and natural boundaries like rivers or city limits
options.D: A shared hobby or professional career path

explanation: Think 'geo' for geography and 'political' for borders. It's simply a community defined by clear lines on a map, like a Local Government Area!

question: How do rapid diagnostic tests help in the fight against antibiotic resistance?

options.A: By increasing the potency of standard penicillin doses
options.B: By curing viral colds without needing any medication
options.C: By killing all resistant bacteria instantly on contact
options.D: By distinguishing viral infections from bacterial ones

explanation: Quick tests show if an illness is viral, stopping doctors from prescribing unnecessary antibiotics (since antibiotics don't touch viruses!).

question: What is the main job of anabolism in the body?

options.A: Breaking down large food particles into waste
options.B: Destroying damaged cells through natural pathways
options.C: Building complex molecules from simpler ones
options.D: Releasing stored heat directly into the bloodstream

explanation: Think of anabolism as the builder! It takes small building blocks and puts them together to form larger, complex molecules, just like building a house with bricks.

question: Why is drying the newborn baby immediately after birth a critical nursing action?

options.A: To stimulate the baby to learn how to walk
options.B: To remove the vernix completely so the skin breathes
options.C: To check for hidden birthmarks and bruises
options.D: To prevent heat loss and hypothermia

explanation: Wet skin combined with room air causes rapid evaporation and heat loss, which can lead to dangerous cold stress in newborns. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h3)

question: Why could it backfire if you only consult wealthy community elites when planning a health project?

options.A: Elites are immune to most common infectious and tropical diseases
options.B: The elites may not represent or understand the actual needs of marginalized groups
options.C: Traditional leaders always forbid modern nursing practices in public spaces
options.D: The local government will fine the clinic for bypassing traditional protocols

explanation: It's easy to miss the struggles of the everyday person if you only talk to the wealthy leaders. Great nurses make sure to listen to voices from every corner of the community!

question: What is the main goal of providing nutrition care for patients in the hospital?

options.A: Preventing malnutrition and supporting healing
options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital food services
options.C: Replacing the need for doctor-ordered diets
options.D: Ensuring patients gain weight during every stay

explanation: Great job! Good nutrition keeps the body strong so it can fight off infections and heal wounds faster.

question: What is the main type of tissue you will find in the hypodermis?

options.A: Adipose tissue
options.B: Skeletal muscle
options.C: Dense regular tissue
options.D: Stratified epithelium

explanation: Correct! The hypodermis is packed with adipose (fat) tissue, which helps keep us warm, stores energy, and cushions us from bumps.

question: What do we call a drug's special superpower of harming bacteria without damaging human cells?

options.A: Broad spectrum
options.B: Bacteriostatic action
options.C: Selective toxicity
options.D: Acquired resistance

explanation: You got it! Selective toxicity means the drug safely attacks unique parts of the bacteria while sparing our own human cells.

question: A low blood pressure warning pops up on your bedside monitor screen. Which computer cycle stage just happened?

options.A: Storage
options.B: Output
options.C: Input
options.D: Collection

explanation: Output is what the computer shows back to you on a screen or printer after it finishes processing the data.

question: What happens to an ATP molecule after it gives energy to a cell?

options.A: It loses a phosphate group and turns into ADP
options.B: It gains an extra nitrogen atom and becomes a lipid
options.C: It splits entirely into four separate water molecules
options.D: It binds permanently to a red blood cell for transport

explanation: When ATP spends its energy, it releases one of its phosphate groups and becomes ADP (adenosine diphosphate). It is like a spent battery waiting to be recharged!

question: Which defense mechanism involves unconsciously pushing painful memories away so you don't have to think about them?

options.A: Repression
options.B: Sublimation
options.C: Regression
options.D: Projection

explanation: Repression is like sweeping painful memories under the mental rug without even realizing you're doing it. Out of sight, out of mind!

question: What is St. John's Wort most commonly used for?

options.A: Chronic high blood pressure
options.B: Mild to moderate depression
options.C: Bacterial respiratory infections
options.D: Severe acute schizophrenia

question: How do occupational health programs differ from regular hospital care?

options.A: They only handle severe physical trauma and surgeries

options.C: They ignore mental health and focus strictly on machinery
options.D: They are managed exclusively by financial auditors

question: Which parts of the cell contain the tools needed to turn cholesterol into steroid hormones?

question: What does 'coffee-ground emesis' (vomit that looks like coffee grounds) usually tell you during an assessment?

options.D: First-degree tear

question: Which of these traits tells us that a material is hazardous waste?

options.A: Biodegradable

options.D: Transparent

question: Why is keeping a strict eye on temperature so important when storing and transporting food?

question: What common home habit frequently leads to accidental drug poisoning in communities?

question: What kind of vaginal odor is classically tied to bacterial vaginosis?

question: A patient catches malaria after being bitten by an infected mosquito. How would you classify this transmission?

options.A: Direct contact transmission

options.D: Vehicle-borne transmission

question: Where is the best place to store raw poultry inside a refrigerator to avoid contamination?

options.A: On the lowest shelf
options.B: Directly beside the cooked meals

options.D: Inside the vegetable crisper drawer

question: An outsourced cleaning company constantly fails to clean the wards on time. What should hospital management do?

options.A: Ignore the issue to maintain a peaceful relationship with the private company

question: Which hormone surge directly triggers the release of an egg?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.C: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.D: Luteinizing hormone

question: Why is an ECG called a non-invasive test?

options.A: It is performed entirely on the skin without surgical cuts or entering the body

options.C: It requires general anesthesia to keep the patient calm during the procedure

question: Which chemical is mainly responsible for opening up blood vessels during inflammation?

options.A: Pepsin
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Histamine
options.D: Insulin

question: Why do nurses ask patients about how many pads or tampons they use when assessing heavy periods?

options.A: It reveals the exact day ovulation occurred during the previous month.

question: How does quality improvement differ from traditional quality assurance?

options.A: Quality improvement ignores patient outcomes to focus entirely on financial savings.
options.B: Quality assurance is only used in surgical units, while quality improvement is used everywhere.
options.C: Quality improvement looks at fixing underlying processes, while quality assurance often focuses on finding faults after they happen.
options.D: Quality assurance focuses on ongoing system redesign, while quality improvement looks for individual faults.

explanation: Great job thinking this through! Old-school quality assurance usually looks backward to find someone to blame, but quality improvement looks forward to fix the process so it works smoothly.

question: You want to give mothers at a busy immunization clinic a portable guide on home care for diarrhea. What should you use?

options.A: A flannel graph

options.D: A giant billboard

explanation: Leaflets and brochures are great because mothers can easily slip them into their bags, take them home, and check the care steps later.

question: When a study is called 'empirical,' what kind of information is the researcher using?

options.A: Ancient cultural traditions and habits
options.B: Personal opinions and unproven gut feelings
options.C: Strictly theoretical guesses without testing

question: What is the main reason why hospitals and wards have policies?

options.A: To direct daily clinical actions and standardize care

question: What famous milestone did James Lind achieve when he tested citrus fruits on sailors?

options.A: The chemical isolation of pure vitamin C in a laboratory

options.D: The discovery of complex carbohydrates in grains

question: Which skill is becoming essential for nurses practicing in modern digital health?

options.A: Ability to manufacture smartphones

options.D: Advanced software programming and coding skills

question: Why is recording an accurate pregnancy history so important for an expectant mother?

options.C: It identifies if her past pregnancies put her at a higher medical risk now.

question: Which maternal blood vessels are opened up by the placenta to bathe the fetal villi in nutrient-rich blood?

options.A: Cardinal veins
options.B: Uterine veins

options.D: Spiral arteries

question: What is the primary purpose of a pre-leave nursing risk assessment?

options.A: To ensure the patient no longer requires follow-up care

explanation: A quick risk check helps nurses spot potential dangers and makes sure everyone has a solid backup plan if things get tough.

question: What ethical balance must nurses maintain while collecting data during a disaster?

question: Up to what level should the nurse fill the Nelson inhaler jar with boiling water?

question: How does breastfeeding help a mother's body immediately after delivery?

options.A: It prevents all future menstrual cycles permanently

options.D: It stimulates uterine contractions to reduce postpartum bleeding

question: Which needle gauge range is most appropriate for an intradermal injection?

question: Why do nurses need to know normal pelvic anatomy?

question: How does the muscle type in the oesophagus change from the top down?

question: What is the main reason nurses use portable monitors in the hospital?

question: Why has the demand for formal geriatric homes been on the rise lately?

question: What happens if a computer has physical parts (hardware) but no software?

question: What is another common name for the channels connecting the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle?

question: Which vital sign signs are classic for someone with uncontrolled hyperthyroidism?

question: Why do public health agencies heavily prioritize maternal and child health?

question: How can a nurse manager best build trust and motivation on a busy ward?

question: Why is it important to check cultural or religious guidelines before doing post-mortem care?

question: Which of these is a common informal support system in many Nigerian communities?

question: Why do ketone bodies form when a patient lacks adequate insulin?

question: Why is a budget considered such an important financial tool?

question: Why is taking off (doffing) your PPE safely such a big deal for nurses?

question: How does evaluation help ensure the sustainability of a health project?

question: Which type of drug works mainly by swelling up with water to stretch the intestinal wall and trigger movement?

question: In nursing, what does supporting the 'second victim' mean?

question: What do Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) focus on when you are checking a patient's functional health?

question: A nurse notices a sudden jump in malaria cases during the rainy season. What kind of transmission is this?

question: What is the primary danger of leaving a needle stuck in a multidose vaccine vial?

question: Which task fits best with the work of a community dietitian?

question: A patient asks you (the nurse) to hang out after they leave the hospital. Why is this a bad idea?

question: Which statement best captures the dimensional approach to mental health?

question: Why do nurse leaders use core management functions during a busy shift?

question: Which of these duties should a registered nurse NEVER delegate to an untrained ward assistant?

question: Why do family caregivers often get so stressed or upset when a sick patient refuses to eat?
